title: Как Сеня устраивался на работу  (How Senya Got Hired)

segments.t: Back in the kitchen, Max beats himself up for constantly making a fool of himself in front of Chef Barinov. To cheer him up, Senya and Fedya assure him that every single cook in the kitchen has screwed up before the Chef, and Senya flashes back to his own chaotic job interview years ago.
Мы все когда-то перед ним лажали.
Настоящему повару никакой резюме не требуется.
Ну ты здесь посиди, а я сейчас.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'Oh come on, relax.' Chef Viktor addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'relax'. Nastya answers right away.
'Man, I really am some kind of idiot.' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'damn' and 'I' in a few short words.
'I am always screwing up in front of the Chef.' The meaning hinges on 'always' working together with 'to mess up' in spoken Russian.
Мы все когда-то перед ним лажали.
'Every one of us has screwed up in front of him at some point.' Notice how Russian expresses 'we' and 'to mess up' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Do not sweat it.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'not' before landing on 'to steam oneself in a bathhouse'.
'You bet we have.' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'then' without extra filler words.
'Here is my resume.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'there you go' before landing on 'résumé'. Nastya answers right away.
Настоящему повару никакой резюме не требуется.
'A real cook does not need any resume.' Here Nastya anchors the thought on 'real, genuine' and finishes on 'to be required, be needed', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
'You can tell right away by looking in his eyes.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'him' and finishing on 'eye'.
'I saw your potential immediately.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'potential' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Welcome to the team, son.' The meaning hinges on 'good' working together with 'son' in spoken Russian.
'Thank you, Chef.' Notice how Russian expresses 'thank you' and 'chef' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Ну ты здесь посиди, а я сейчас.

'Well, sit right here, and I will be right back.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'any minute' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Мы все когда-то перед ним лажали.
Настоящему повару никакой резюме не требуется.
Ну ты здесь посиди, а я сейчас.
That wraps up this scene as to cheer Max up after his blunder in front of the Chef, Senya and Fedya recall how they each screwed up on their very first day in Barinov's kitchen. Until next time!
